BERNARDO CARVALHO, PIOTR OPROCHA, AND ELIAS REGO
Proof of Theorem 3.7. First, note that fA has a unique measure of maximal entropy
η and its push forward measure µ = π∗η is a measure of maximal entropy of gA,
because π is bounded to one which guarantees hµ(gA) = hη(fA) (e.g. see [39])
and, hence, h(gA) = h(fA) = hη(fA) = hµ(gA) (see [25] for the definition of metric
entropy).
Next let us prove the uniqueness of the measure of maximal entropy of gA. To do
so, let us fix any measure of maximal entropy ˆµ for gA. Theorem 2.12 implies that
gA has the periodic specification property, which ensures the existence of a sequence
ˆµn of measures supported on periodic points pn such that ˆµ is the weak* limit of
ˆµn (see [25, Proposition 21.8]). Let qn be any periodic point qn ∈π−1(pn) and let
ˆηn be the measure supported on qn. Then ˆµn = π∗(ˆηn). Without loss of generality
we may assume that (ˆηn)n∈N converge in the weak* topology to a measure ˆη. But
then, by continuity of the push-forward operator π∗we have π∗ˆη = ˆµ and as a
consequence
h(gA) = hˆµ(gA) ≤hˆη(fA) ≤h(fA) = h(gA).
This proves that ˆη = η and consequently that ˆµ = µ, that is, µ is the unique
measure of maximal entropy of gA.
